Loss-of-function mutations in SDHA impair the function of the succinate dehydrogenase complex, leading to reduced mitochondrial ATP synthesis. This energetic deficit, coupled with potential accumulation of succinate, disrupts multiple cellular processes in neurons, ultimately manifesting as neurodegeneration, ataxia, and optic atrophy.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a patient with pathogenic SDHA variants but lacking any of the core phenotypes (neurodegeneration, ataxia, optic atrophy) would falsify this hypothesis.
